# Checks

For anyone choosing or tuning a project's settings: every check the engine ships, with its default level and parameters.

<!-- Generated by tools/render-checks.py from the engine's check manifest. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each check has a level: `off`, `warn` or `error`. At `error`, a check reports what it finds as written, errors and warnings both; at `warn`, every error becomes a warning; `off` skips it. A check whose Ratchet row says yes reports its size limits as warnings, and the ratchet turns a new or grown breach into an error. Set a level or a parameter under `[checks.<id>]` in `.context-gate/config.toml`. A lower level or a limit moved in its looser direction needs a `reason`; a list widened in its looser direction is reported until it has one. See [configuration.md](configuration.md) for the syntax and [how-it-works.md](how-it-works.md) for the model. `govern explain <id>` prints a check's effective settings in your project.

| Check | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`registry`](#registry) | `error` | Every registry entry is well formed: its required facts present, a known tier, ID facts where decisions are kept, and every fact where the configuration reads it. |
| [`id-ranges`](#id-ranges) | `error` | Decision-ID ranges claimed by the workspace and each project never overlap. |
| [`checkout-hygiene`](#checkout-hygiene) | `off` | Checkouts in the configured registry roles carry none of the governance root's own files, and their upstream remote matches the registry. |

| [`trap-entries`](#trap-entries) | `warn` | Every trap entry says when it bites: the **Bites when:** line is what the trap index shows. |
| [`doc-frontmatter`](#doc-frontmatter) | `error` | Every governed doc carries valid frontmatter, a current review date, and resolvable related links; working files carry a status and stay bounded. |
| [`workspace-docs`](#workspace-docs) | `error` | The workspace's own docs exist and pass the same doc check as project docs. |

## Registry and checkouts

The projects a governance root covers, the facts recorded about each, and the repositories they live in.

### `registry`

Every registry entry is well formed: its required facts present, a known tier, ID facts where decisions are kept, and every fact where the configuration reads it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` (fixed core: can be `warn` or `error`, never `off`) |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Where does your registry keep each fact about a project, and which tiers do you use?

**Why:** A key the engine looks for in the wrong place is a check that silently never runs.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `required_keys` | list | `["name", "dir", "tier"]` | a value is removed | Facts every registry entry carries |
| `tiers` | list | `["full", "registered"]` | a value is added | Allowed tier values |

### `id-ranges`

Decision-ID ranges claimed by the workspace and each project never overlap.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do projects share one decision-ID namespace?

**Why:** Two logs that can mint the same ID make every citation ambiguous.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `checkout-hygiene`

Checkouts in the configured registry roles carry none of the governance root's own files, and their upstream remote matches the registry.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `off` |
| Scope | Runs once per project |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do you govern checkouts of repositories you don't want your governance files to land in (a fork you send pull requests from, a repo you publish)? Which registry roles are they, and which files must never appear in them?

**Why:** A governance file inside a fork lands in somebody else's pull request; inside a published repo it lands in a release. Both failures are silent.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roles` | list | `[]` | — | Registry roles whose checkouts are checked |
| `forbidden` | list | `[]` | a value is removed | Paths, relative to a checkout, that never belong in it |
| `rules` | table | `{}` | — | Decision id to cite per role, e.g. { contribute = "W-1" } |
| `upstream_remote` | str | `"upstream"` | — | Remote whose URL must equal the registry's upstream |
| `setup_hint` | str | `""` | — | What to run when a checkout or remote is missing |

### `agent-worktrees`

Where agents run, each checkout's own repo ignores `.claude/worktrees/`, so an agent's worktree is never committed into it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once per project; also runs against the workspace's own files |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do agents in this workspace work in their own worktrees (Claude Code's `isolation: "worktree"`), and should each checkout's repo keep those worktrees out of its commits?

**Why:** An agent worktree is a nested checkout under `.claude/worktrees/`; a repo that does not ignore it sweeps it into the next `git add -A` as an embedded repo, silently. A user's global excludes file does not count, since other clones lack it; a repo's own `.git/info/exclude` still does, but only `.gitignore` protects every clone, so that is the fix.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `licences`

Every registry entry declares a licence, and each configured conflict (say, copyleft code beside permissive code) is recorded as a workspace decision.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `off` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do repos under different licences share this workspace? Which combinations need a recorded decision about how code stays separated?

**Why:** A licence firewall depends on knowing every licence, and on the reasoning being written down where the next session will find it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `require_declared` | bool | `true` | — | Every registry entry declares a licence |
| `rule` | str | `""` | — | Decision id to cite when a licence is undeclared |
| `conflicts` | list of tables | `[]` | — | Pairings that need a recorded decision. Keys: `a`, `b`, `decision`. |

## Decision logs and traps

Numbered decision entries (`## P-12 — Title`) and trap entries (`## T-3 — Title`).

### `decision-log`

Decision entries are well-formed, unique, in range and in order, carry a known status and the required fields, and stay short.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory; also runs against the workspace's own files |
| Ratchet | Yes: size breaches are recorded in the baseline |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which statuses and fields does a decision entry need, and how long may one be?

**Why:** The log is read by index; an entry the index cannot see, or one that is really a design doc, defeats that.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_words` | int | `250` | raised | Words per entry before it is flagged |
| `statuses` | list | `["locked", "provisional", "deferred"]` | a value is added | Allowed **Status:** values (case-insensitive). There is no 'superseded': a replaced decision becomes a one-line pointer |
| `required_fields` | list | `["Rule", "Why"]` | a value is removed | Bold fields every entry carries, e.g. **Rule:** |
| `ascending` | bool | `true` | — | Entries must appear in ascending id order |

### `decision-history`

A decision entry's body carries no history label — a rewritten entry states only today's rule.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory; also runs against the workspace's own files |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** When a decision entry is rewritten, does it ever keep a line naming what it used to say?

**Why:** An agent reading the entry pays for something no longer true; git already keeps the old text.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` | list | `["Earlier", "Previously", "Formerly", "Superseded", "Was"]` | a value is removed | History labels flagged at the start of a body line, bold (`**Earlier:**`) or plain (`Earlier:`) |

### `trap-ids`

A trap id is owned by exactly one of a project's trap files.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do your projects split traps across more than one file?

**Why:** The same id in two files leaves `show`, `find` and `trap-add` no principled way to pick.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `trap-entries`

Every trap entry says when it bites: the **Bites when:** line is what the trap index shows.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Do your trap entries carry a **Bites when:** line?

**Why:** An entry without one shows as a dash in the index, so nobody reading the index can tell whether it applies to them.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

## Docs

The governed docs: their frontmatter, count, links, generated index blocks and wording.

### `doc-frontmatter`

Every governed doc carries valid frontmatter, a current review date, and resolvable related links; working files carry a status and stay bounded.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | Yes: size breaches are recorded in the baseline |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which frontmatter keys, doc types and working-file statuses do your docs use, and how often should control and reference docs be reviewed?

**Why:** Frontmatter is what tells an agent whether and when to open a doc.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `required_keys` | list | `["doc_type", "purpose", "audience", "load_when", "last_reviewed"]` | a value is removed | Frontmatter keys every governed doc carries |
| `doc_types` | list | `["control", "reference", "working"]` | a value is added | Allowed doc_type values |
| `audiences` | list | `["agent", "human", "both"]` | a value is added | Allowed audience values |
| `working_statuses` | list | `["active", "held", "planned", "complete", "superseded"]` | a value is added, or emptied | A working file's status must start with one of these; empty allows free text |
| `stale_days` | int | `120` | raised | Days since last_reviewed before a review is due |
| `stale_types` | list | `["control", "reference"]` | — | doc_types that go stale; working files are curated instead |
| `max_working_words` | int | `6000` | raised | Words in a working file before it is flagged |

### `workspace-docs`

The workspace's own docs exist and pass the same doc check as project docs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which docs does the workspace root require, and which does it govern?

**Why:** The layer that governs everything else is governed by the same rules.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `governed-doc-count`

Bounds how many governed docs a project carries.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | Yes: size breaches are recorded in the baseline |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** How many governed docs should a project need before it is time to merge or archive some?

**Why:** The doc system should stay possible to grow without growing by habit.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_docs` | int | `14` | raised | Governed docs per project |

### `doc-set`

A project whose tier requires governance carries the full doc set.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which docs must every governed project carry?

**Why:** A missing doc is discovered by the gate, not by the agent that needed it.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `generated-blocks`

Every configured generated block exists, holds its markers, and matches what `index` would write.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root; under `check --project X`, runs for that one project |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which docs carry generated index blocks?

**Why:** The block is what an agent reads to decide which doc to open; a stale one sends it to the wrong file or hides one.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `writing-rules`

Files matching the configured globs contain none of the configured strings.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `off` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Is there copy with a house style you must enforce (drafts that go to another project, public docs)? Which files, and which words or characters are out?

**Why:** A style guide is only a rule if something enforces it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `files` | list | `[]` | — | Globs, relative to the governance root |
| `rules` | list of tables | `[]` | — | One per forbidden string. Keys: `text`, `use` (optional), `why` (optional), `level` (optional), `ignore_case` (optional). |

### `stale-references`

Governed docs no longer mention paths the install moved or retired, or names the project retired.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Has your project retired names or paths that docs may still mention? What replaced them?

**Why:** A doc that points at something gone sends the next reader to the wrong place.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | list of tables | `[]` | — | Retired names and what replaced them. Keys: `text`, `now`. |

### `doc-links`

Every relative link in a governed doc points at a file that exists.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root; under `check --project X`, runs for that one project |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Should broken links between your docs fail the gate?

**Why:** A link to nothing sends the next reader, human or agent, to guess.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `doc-reachability`

Every governed doc is listed in the project's generated doc registry.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Should every doc be reachable from the project's index?

**Why:** An agent finds a doc through the index; one the index does not list is a doc nobody opens.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | str | `"INDEX.md"` | — | The doc that carries the doc-registry block, relative to the governance dir |

## Working files

A project's working-files directory and its HANDOFF.

### `working-file-count`

Bounds how many files sit directly in a project's working-files directory.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** How many working files may a project hold at once?

**Why:** The directory filling up is the failure, independent of any one file's length.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_files` | int | `12` | raised | Files directly under the working dir |
| `extensions` | list | `["*.md", "*.html", "*.pdf"]` | — | Which files count |

### `finished-files`

A working file whose status says it is finished should be deleted once it has sat untouched for a few days. A finished file that was never committed is flagged at once instead, so it is committed before it is deleted.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which statuses mean finished, and how long may a finished file linger?

**Why:** Git keeps the history, so nothing is lost by deleting a finished file once it has been committed, and nothing is gained by every sweep re-reading it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_days` | int | `7` | raised | Days a finished file may sit untouched |
| `finished_statuses` | list | `["complete", "superseded"]` | a value is removed | Statuses that mean the file is finished |
| `exempt` | list | `["HANDOFF.md", "traps*"]` | a value is added | File names never treated as finished (glob patterns) |

### `handoff-words`

Bounds a project's HANDOFF: a snapshot of where things stand, not a log.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once per project, for each project with a governed tier and a governance directory |
| Ratchet | Yes: size breaches are recorded in the baseline |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** How long may a HANDOFF grow before it needs trimming?

**Why:** A HANDOFF that keeps growing across sessions stops being read.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_words` | int | `1500` | raised | Words in a HANDOFF |

## Agents, skills and Claude Code

Agent and skill definitions, hooks, and the Claude Code memory index.

### `agents`

Every agent definition pins its name, model, effort and whether it may read CLAUDE.md, an optional turn cap stays under the ceiling, and prose never contradicts the cap.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Which frontmatter keys does every agent carry, is a turn cap required, and what is the most turns any agent may run?

**Why:** An agent riding on defaults is one nobody controls; a cap, where one is set, is a ceiling that surfaces a non-converging agent, and a cap stated twice is invisible drift.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `required_keys` | list | `["description", "model", "effort", "omitClaudeMd"]` | a value is removed | Frontmatter every agent carries besides name and maxTurns |
| `warn_keys` | list | `["omitClaudeMd"]` | a value is added | Keys in required_keys that only warn when absent; a profile sets this to [] to make them errors |
| `efforts` | list | `["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]` | a value is added | Allowed effort values |
| `require_max_turns` | bool | `false` | — | Whether every agent must set maxTurns |
| `max_turns` | int | `0` | raised | Ceiling on maxTurns, 0 for no ceiling |

### `skills`

Every skill definition has frontmatter with a description.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Does this project define its own Claude Code skills?

**Why:** Claude Code skips a skill without a description, silently.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skills_dir` | str | `".claude/skills"` | — | Where the project's skills live |

### `memory-index`

Bounds the Claude Code memory index for this project.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** How many lines may the memory index hold before it needs pruning?

**Why:** The index is loaded into every session; measure what you want bounded.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_lines` | int | `40` | raised | Non-blank lines in MEMORY.md |

### `hooks-wired`

Each configured hook script exists and is wired in .claude/settings.json on its event and matcher.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `off` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Does any rule of yours rely on a Claude Code hook (blocking outbound actions, guarding a tool)? Which script, on which event and matcher?

**Why:** A rule enforced by a hook is only a rule while the hook is wired; a malformed settings file disables every hook in it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Looser when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | str | `".claude/settings.json"` | — | Settings file the hooks live in |
| `hooks` | list of tables | `[]` | — | Hooks that must be wired. Keys: `script`, `event`, `matcher`, `rule` (optional), `missing` (optional), `unwired` (optional). |

## The ratchet and overrides

The rules about the rules: recorded breaches, and settings that differ from the standard.

### `ratchet`

A size breach not recorded in the baseline, or one that grew past its record, is an error.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `error` (fixed core: can be `warn` or `error`, never `off`) |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root; under `check --project X`, runs for that one project |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** (Not optional.) Existing breaches are recorded at adoption; new ones must be fixed or accepted on purpose.

**Why:** A warning nobody acts on is not a softer rule; it is a rule that stopped functioning.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

### `standard-overrides`

Every format setting that differs from the standard, every setting that differs from the project's profile, and every list setting widened past what it inherited, says why.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.0 |

**Question:** Where does this project keep a format or a setting that differs from the standard or its profile, or a list widened past what either sets, and why?

**Why:** One standard, met or overridden on purpose: an override with no reason is a fork nobody decided to keep.

No parameters: set its `level` only.

## Other checks

### `git-repo`

The governance root is inside a git repository.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default level | `warn` |
| Scope | Runs once for the governance root |
| Ratchet | No |
| Since | 0.4.1 |

**Question:** Is this project a git repository? Several checks read its history.

**Why:** Outside git, the checks that read history or ignore rules (when a file was last touched, whether it was ever committed, what git ignores) quietly check nothing; the gate would look green while not looking.

No parameters: set its `level` only.
